questions.question: How do you install a third party module?
questions.solution_html:
• Use NPM:`npm install ` (local, adds to `package.json` dependencies). (1.5)
  • Example:`npm installexpress` ,(For specific version: `npm install express@4.x`) (1.5)
  • Global Scope
  • In Browser Environment: Any variable declared with `var` outside a function becomes a
  • global variable and isattached to the`window` object.
  • Example
  • var x= 10; // Global
  • console.log(window.x); // 10
  • All scripts inthesame HTMLpage sharethesame global scope.
  • In Node.js Environment: Each JavaScript file is treated as a separate module. Variables
  • declared at the top level (using `var`, `let`, or `const`) are local to that module (Module
  • Scope), not global. They are not added tothe`global` object.
  • Example
  • var x= 10; // Modulescoped (onlyavailable inthis file)
  • console.log(global.x); //undefined
  • Tocreateatrue global variable inNode.js, we mustexplicitly use
  • global.myVar="Hello"; //Trueglobal
  • async keyword: Used before a function declaration. It tells JavaScript that the function
  • always returns a Promise.
  • Organized File Storage: Proper directory structure helps to organize different types of
  • files such as user uploads, log files, configuration files, static assets (images, CSS, JS)
  • and temporary files.This makes theapplication cleaner andeasier to maintain.
  • Synchronous Mechanism (Blocking)
  •  Operations are performed synchronously.Theprogram waits until thefileoperation is
  • completed.
  •  Not recommended for web servers as it blocksthe event loop.
  • Example
  • const fs= require('fs');
  • //Reading afile
  • const data =fs.readFileSync('file.txt', 'utf8');
  • console.log(data);
  • //Writingafile
  • fs.writeFileSync('file.txt','Hello World');
  • res.send()Sends aresponse ofvarious types (string, object, array,etc.).
questions.final_answer: res.send()Sends aresponse ofvarious types (string, object, array,etc.)

questions.question: What is global installation in NPM?
questions.solution_html:
• Global installation makes the package available system-wide (usable from any directory via
  • CLI). (1.5)
  • Command: `npm install -g ` (e.g., `npm install -g nodemon`). Installed in
  • global `node_modules`. (1.5)
  • Use for tools/utilities, not project dependencies. (1.5)
  • [Give fullmarks for any2points]
  • Function Scope
  • In both Browser and Node.js: Variables declared with `var` inside a function have function
  • scope (accessible anywhereinsidethat function, even before declaration due to hoisting).
  • `let` and`const` have block scope inboth environments.
  • The main difference appears in top-level code. In Node.js, top-level code is wrapped insidea
  • modulewrapper function, so itbehaves likefunction scope.
  • [Introduction to Scope + mentioning Global Scope difference – (2 marks). Detailed
  • explanation of Global Scope in Browser vs Node.js with examples – (2 marks). Function
  • Scope explanation (similarity+top-level difference) –(1mark)]
  • await keyword: Can only be used inside an async function. It pauses the execution of
  • thefunction until thePromiseis resolved orrejected.
  • Example: asyncfunction getUserData() {
  • try{
  • let response=awaitfetch('https://api.example.com/user');
  • let user = awaitresponse.json();
  • console.log(user);
  • }
  • catch (error){
  • console.log("Erroroccurred:", error);
  • }}
  • getUserData();
  • Advantages of async/await
  •  Improved Readability: Thecode looks simpleand linear,making it easy tounderstand the
  • flow.
  •  BetterError Handling:Wecan usethenormal try catch block for error handling.
  •  Easier Debugging: Debugging is simplercompared to callbacks orpromisechains.
  •  Sequential Execution:Helps to write asynchronous operations in astep-by-step manner.
  •  Less Complex Code: Reduces nesting and makes thecode moremaintainable.
  • [Definitionof async/await -(1mark) +Explanation ofasync andawaitkeywords2 Marks +Clear
  • code example (2Marks) + At least4advantages -(2 marks): Maximum (5Marks)]
  • User Data Management: Servers often need to store user-specific data (e.g., profile
  • pictures, documents). Dynamic directory creation allows each user to have their own
  • folder,improvingdata organization and security.
  • Asynchronous Mechanism(Non-Blocking)-Recommended
  •  Operations are performed asynchronouslyusing callbacks orpromises.
  •  Theprogram does not wait and continues executing othercode.
  • Examples
  • Reading afileasynchronously
  • const fs= require('fs');
  • fs.readFile('file.txt','utf8',(err,data)=> {
  • if(err) throw err;
  • console.log(data);
  • });
  • Writingafileasynchronously
  • fs.writeFile('file.txt','WelcometoNode.js',(err) => {
  • if(err) throw err;
  • console.log('Filewritten successfully');
  • });
  • [Introduction to fs module + Synchronous vs Asynchronous (2 Marks), Explanation with code
  • examples of reading and writing (Sync + Async) (2 Marks), Advantages of Async over Sync – 1
  • Mark]
  • res.json() — Sends a JSON response. Automatically sets the Content-Type header to
  • application/json.
  • Example
  • app.get('/api/user', (req, res)=> {
  • res.json({ name: "Biju", age: 22,city:"Kollam"});
  • });

questions.question: What is thread-based request handling?
questions.solution_html:
• Traditional web servers (e.g., Apache) use a thread-per-request model: each request spawns
  • a new thread, which can lead to high memory use and context-switching overhead under
  • load. Node.js uses asingle-threaded, event-driven, non-blocking model instead.
  • + example (1mark)]
  • Application Scalability: As the application grows, directory management helps in
  • handling large volumes offiles efficiently without cluttering theroot folder.
  • res.status()—Sets theHTTPstatus code for theresponse.
  • Example
  • app.get('/notfound',(req, res)=> {
  • res.status(404).send("PageNot Found");
  • });

questions.question: Describe the purpose of req and res objects in HTTP communication.
questions.solution_html:
• req(Request): Represents the incoming HTTP request from the client. Contains properties
  • like`req.url`, `req.method`, `req.headers`, `req.params`, `req.query`, `req.body`.
  • + anyoneproperty .(5mark)]
  • res (Response): Used to send the HTTP response back to the client. Methods like
  • `res.send()`, `res.json()`, `res.status()`, `res.end()`.
  • + anyoneproperty .(5mark)]
  • Temporary File Handling: Many server operations require temporary directories for
  • processing files (e.g., file uploads, report generation). These can be created and deleted
  • after use.
  • res.redirect() —Redirects theclient toadifferent URL.
  • Example
  • app.get('/old-page',(req, res)=> {
  • res.redirect('/new-page'); //Default 302redirect
  • //res.redirect(301, '/new-page'); // Permanent redirect
  • });
  • OtherUseful Methods
  •  res.sendFile() →Send afile (e.g., image, PDF)
  •  res.render()→Render templateengines (likePug/EJS)
  •  res.end()→Endthe responseprocess
  • [Introductiontoresobject -(1mark), Explanation+ examples any4methods -(4 marks)]

questions.question: Why is EventEmitter important in asynchronous programming?
questions.solution_html:
• `EventEmitter` (from `events` module)enables event-driven architecture. (1)
  • Emit customevents (`emitter.emit('event')`) andlisten (`emitter.on('event', callback)`). (1)
  • It supports loose coupling, handles async operations (e.g., file read completion, DB events)
  • without blocking, and is core to Node.js's non-blocking model. (1)
  • Integration with Web Features: Directories are essential for serving static files (using
  • express.static()), managing templates, and working with URLmodules forfile routing.
  • In Node.js, functions like fs.mkdir(), fs.readdir(), fs.rmdir(), and fs.promises are used for
  • directory operations.
  • [Introduction to directory management in server-side (Node.js) (1mark) + Explanation of
  • importance(any 4points)(3Marks) + fsmodule functions(any 2)–(1mark)]
